issues.description: Method addGuestStudents(int): the UML in the problem statement declares addGuestStudents(int) with return type void, but the reference solution implements public boolean addGuestStudents(int ...). The template does not provide a concrete signature (only a TODO). This discrepancy leaves students uncertain which return type to implement and whether the method should signal success/failure via a boolean or be void as documented in the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected signature explicit and consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) update the UML and problem text to declare addGuestStudents(int): boolean and explain semantics (e.g., returns true on success, false on invalid input), and update the template to include the boolean signature; or (B) change the solution implementation to match the UML by making addGuestStudents(int) return void (and handle invalid input via no-op or documented behavior), and also add that void signature to the template. In all cases, update the template Lecture.java to include the chosen method signature so students know exactly which return type to implement.
